You will read ten short passages from UK legislation and from a GOV.UK guide about the Winter Fuel Payment.
For each passage, write ONE plain English sentence that states the rule the passage makes, for one person called
the applicant (the passages call this person "P" or "you").

Some dates and amounts have fixed names, listed at the end. When your sentence mentions one of them, use its name
exactly as listed (the words in quotes). Otherwise write the sentence as you think best. Write each sentence on its
own; do not refer to the other passages.

Answer with exactly ten lines and nothing else, one per passage, in this form:
1. <your sentence>
2. <your sentence>
...

Definitions from the same sources:
- “qualifying week” means in respect of any year the week beginning on the third Monday in the September of that year;
- The amount you get is based on when you were born and your circumstances between 21 to 27 September 2026. This is called the ‘qualifying week’.

Passage 1 (S1 reg. 2(a)):
2. Subject to regulation 4, the Secretary of State must pay a winter fuel payment out of the social fund to a person (“P”) where—
(a)in or before the qualifying week, P has reached pensionable age, and

Passage 2 (S1 reg. 2(b)):
2. Subject to regulation 4, the Secretary of State must pay a winter fuel payment out of the social fund to a person (“P”) where—
(b)in respect of any day falling within the qualifying week, P is ordinarily resident in England or Wales.

Passage 3 (S1 reg. 3(1)):
3.—(1) Subject to paragraphs (2) and (3), where P has not reached the age of 80 in or before the qualifying week, the amount of a winter fuel payment is £200.

Passage 4 (S1 reg. 3(2)):
(2) Where P has not reached the age of 80 in or before the qualifying week, the amount of a winter fuel payment is £100 where—
(a)a relevant benefit has not been, nor falls to be, paid to P in respect of the qualifying week, and
(b)P is—
(i)in that week, living with a person entitled to a winter fuel payment under regulation 2 in respect of the qualifying week, or
(ii)in residential care.

Passage 5 (S1 reg. 3(4)):
(4) Subject to paragraphs (5) and (6), where P has reached the age of 80 in or before the qualifying week, the amount of a winter fuel payment is £300.

Passage 6 (S1 reg. 4(2)(c)):
(2) This paragraph applies where, throughout the qualifying week, P is—
(c)detained in custody under a sentence imposed by a court.

Passage 7 (S1 reg. 4(5) and (6)):
(5) Subject to paragraph (6), this paragraph applies where P has not made a claim for a winter fuel payment on or before the 31st March following the qualifying week.
(6) Paragraph (5) does not apply where—
(a)a winter fuel payment has been made by virtue of regulation 5(1) in respect of the qualifying week, or
(b)regulation 5(2) applies.

Passage 8 (S3 reg. 2(5)):
(5) For the purposes of paragraph (4), a period during which a person is regarded as receiving or having received free in-patient treatment shall be deemed to begin on the day after the day on which he enters a hospital or similar institution referred to in that paragraph and to end on the day on which he leaves such a hospital or similar institution.

Passage 9 (S2 'If your income is over £35,000'):
7. If your income is over £35,000
If your total income is over £35,000, HM Revenue and Customs (HMRC) will take your Winter Fuel Payment back.

Passage 10 (S2:166):
If you do not opt out and your total income is over £35,000, you’ll receive the Winter Fuel Payment but HMRC will take it back.
